Subject: VectorMed MAP: batching & prefetch guardrails for unit-econ checks

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I’ve attached a one-page MAP draft and a starter token-econ CSV so your engineering and procurement teams can see the levers we’ll validate during the POC. Two quick asks up front:

1) Can you confirm a realistic traffic profile (percentages for synchronous patient queries vs. async backfill) for month 1 of the POC? That will determine batching potential.
2) Any constraints on prefetch/caching of patient context (HIPAA-safe token retention windows) we should assume?

The MAP draft calls out a few guardrails we typically use to validate tokens/$:
- Baseline model: redwood/gpt-med-lite (quantized) at 2048 context
- Prefetch horizon: 24 hours (default) — we can tighten to 1 hour if data retention requires
- Batching window: 50–200ms for sync; micro-batching for async up to 500ms
- Acceptance metric: tokens/$ under pilot SLAs and average latency < 180ms for sync 95th pct

I’ve cc’d procurement as requested and included a copy of the CSV (vectormed_token_model_v1.csv) with conservative usage estimates. If you can reply with the traffic split and any retention constraints we’ll run a quick sensitivity sweep and return a MAP appendix that shows optimistic/median/pessimistic tokens-per-dollar.

Thanks —
Diego

Thanks Diego — quick answers below.

Traffic split (expected for POC):
- Sync patient queries (chat-like triage): 60%
- Async clinician batch processing (notes summarization/backfill): 30%
- Background analytics (low priority): 10%

Retention/PHI constraints:
- We can store patient context for prefetching for up to 8 hours in the POC environment (encrypted at rest). Anything beyond that will need a formal review.
- No offloading of raw PHI to third-party caches; caching must use a hashed patient key and truncated context (name/PHI redacted).

Procurement loop: procurement@vectormed.com will want a per-token estimate and a short ops note describing how caching complies with our guardrails.

Diego / Naomi / Markus —

Attached is a quick sensitivity export (I updated vectormed_token_model_v1.csv -> vectormed_token_model_v1_priyom.csv). Highlights:

- Prefetch horizon: moving from 1h -> 8h yields an effective cache hit improvement of ~12 percentage points on our model given VectorMed's query distribution; 24h gives diminishing returns unless patient repeat rate > 70%.
- Sync batching: at 50ms average window we see ~1.1x throughput vs single-request baseline; at 150ms window throughput jumps to ~1.6x; at 300ms you get ~2.0x but p95 latency for sync edges toward our 180ms target. Recommend using 150ms as a pragmatic default for POC.
- Cache hit sensitivity: 0% / 20% / 40% scenarios change tokens per call proportionally; show both per-call tokens and tokens/$ in the appendix.

Technical note on truncated-context caching: hashing + redaction is fine; accuracy impact is <3% on generation quality for our health-domain baseline prompts (we tested on previous pilots). We should include a short ops bullet: "Cache keys are patient-hash + schema-version; stored context is truncated to last N tokens and redaction applied pre-storage."

I attached the CSV and a short appendix draft (first tab) that Diego can share.

Priyom Das
